sentences.text: The crowns of Tuyuria teeth possess a basolingual point that contacts the labial buttress of the neighboring tooth.
Unlike many of its relatives, Tuyuria lacks lateral crown processes on its teeth.
A labial canal opens beneath the labial buttress and links to the pulp cavity within each tooth.
Numerous transverse vascular canals permeate the base of the crowns, indicating a complex internal blood supply.
The tooth crowns exhibit pronounced wear facets that are rare among members of the order Eugeneodontiformes.
The shape of the teeth suggests an adaptation for crushing hard-shelled prey such as crustaceans.
Tuyuria is placed within the superfamily Edestoidei of the order Eugeneodontiformes.
It is the type genus of the newly erected family Lestrodontidae.
Fossils of Tuyuria have been recovered from the Tula Oblast region of Russia.
Some researchers propose that the wear facets record scissor-type shearing between opposing tooth whorls, while others argue they reflect a placement within a parasymphyseal tooth series.
